results.summary_before: This design lights up segments of a seven-segment display to form the letter 'b' with a period at the end. The segments are controlled by switches: switches 1 and 2 control the bottom-right segment (OR logic), switches 3 and 4 control the bottom segment (AND logic), and switches 5-8 control other segments individually. It can be tested by toggling switches and observing the display. External hardware includes an LED display and switches.
results.summary: This design lights LEDs to form the letter 'b' with a period at the end. Switches 1 and 2 use OR-style control for the bottom-right light, switches 3 and 4 use AND-style control for the bottom light, and switches 5-8 each control their own light. It can be tested by toggling switches and observing the lights. External hardware includes an LED display and switches.

results.summary_before: This is a 7-bit priority arbiter that takes seven inputs and asserts at most one of seven outputs, prioritizing the lowest active input. An eighth output toggles with a clock and reset signal. It is tested by connecting outputs to a 7-segment display or LEDs and verifying correct arbitration as inputs change. External hardware includes input switches, a 7-segment LED display, and possibly a button to step the clock.
results.summary: This is a 7-bit priority arbiter that takes seven inputs and asserts at most one of seven outputs, prioritizing the lowest active input. An eighth output stays high while reset_n XOR clk is active, effectively when the clock is low. It is tested by connecting outputs to a 7-segment display or LEDs and verifying correct arbitration as inputs change. External hardware includes input switches, a 7-segment LED display, and possibly a button to step the clock.
